claim: The battery carries the design-case load for 5 days or more without sun
law: Stored energy / daily load, usable 80 % of 154 Wh, load 16 Wh/day (flash, pilot, radio, standby)

claim: At 2.5 peak sun hours the 20 W panel stores at least the daily load
law: Conservation of energy or mass

claim: On a 50 C peak day the cell stays below its 55 C charge limit and the battery charges at least the daily load (CRS-DDR-005)
law: Cell = ambient + shielded rise (3.9 K at 70 deg sun, shield factor 0.25 borrowed); stored 98.7 Wh/day against 16.0; review sensitivity: at 45 deg sun and shield 0.50 the cell reaches 60.1 C and 27.6 Wh/day is still stored

claim: The sun-heated enclosure stays below the 60 C discharge limit of LiFePO4 at 50 C ambient
law: Steady-state balance: absorbed sun (shield factor 0.25, borrowed) plus internal loss over the convection area

claim: The sealed light bar, white finish, stays below the 74 C upper limit of an LED traffic signal module at 50 C ambient in the worst case (CRS-DDR-005)
law: Same method as S4 for a 2 mm aluminium bar, no shield, dusty white (alpha 0.55, assumed), sun at the worst elevation, LEDs flashing continuously; the 74 C figure is a datasheet class figure

claim: Both sides flash within 0.5 s of a trigger, including two radio retries
law: LoRa time on air at SF7 plus processing and acknowledgement timeouts

claim: The 868 MHz link across 15 m with a 25 dB blockage keeps at least 10 dB of margin
law: Free-space path loss plus a blockage allowance against SF7 sensitivity

claim: Radio on-air time in the busiest hour stays inside the 1 % duty cycle of the 868 MHz sub-band
law: Time on air per packet times packets in the busiest hour (the duty-cycle rule is ETSI practice; the US band has other rules, to assess in REG)

claim: Each amber head gives about 3,900 cd on axis, enough to be seen at 100 m in sun
law: Screening from LED power, efficacy and optic efficiency over the beam solid angle gives 3,939 cd; the SAE J595 class figure cited in IA-21 and the heads' photometric data are not checked
check: No calculation closes it at P3; photometry from the datasheet of the heads bought, then a field check

claim: The 114.3 x 3.6 mm post carries sign, panel and enclosure in a 40 m/s gust at 60 % of yield or less
law: Drag force on each part at 980 Pa, bending moment at the base, sigma = M / S against S235 yield

claim: A 1,800 mm embedment in a 500 mm clay footing resists the overturning moment
law: Non-constrained pole footing, IBC 1807.3.2.1 screening, lateral bearing 100 psf per ft of depth (clay, class 5 screening value, assumed)

claim: The M10 anti-rotation through-bolt carries the sign torque on a new post
law: Couple on the two post walls against bolt shear and wall bearing (Eurocode 3 practice, gamma 1.25)

claim: On the smallest existing pole (76 mm) two keyed saddles resist the sign torque
law: Capstan-style friction of a 1,000 N band at friction 0.4 (assumed) on two saddles, against the eccentric gust torque

claim: The LiFePO4 pack charges and discharges safely from -20 to +50 C ambient
law: Charging below 0 C plates lithium, so the BMS must cut charge there (low-temperature cut-off is in BOM line 9); commercial packs list charge 0 to 55 C and discharge -20 to 60 C; fuse at the terminal; vent and fire risk in H2 of CRS-RSK-001
check: Cell datasheet and BMS thresholds to assess when the pack is chosen

claim: The flashing is not a photosensitivity hazard for people beside the beacon
law: Lit area of two heads (174 cm2) seen from 1.5 m is 7.7 msr and from 1.2 m (button 1 m from the pole, bar centre 2.17 m up, eye 1.5 m) about 12 msr, against the 6 msr WCAG 2.1 analogue (no road or clinical standard checked); the IA-21 sequence is five pulses a second inside a sequence; the heads face the road, so the angle from the button reduces the apparent area
check: Fails the analogue screen. Fix proposed: a viewing-angle check, then dim the heads while the button is held or add a pedestrian-end baffle; a road-authority and clinical-safety review is to assess. Moving the bar or dimming is a safety trade-off, so it goes to Amish (O3)

claim: A driver at 60 km/h can stop within the 100 m seeing distance of the warning
law: Stopping distance = u t + u^2 / (2 a), t = 2.5 s (AASHTO design value), a = 3.4 m/s2 (assumed); the 100 m seeing distance is PR-002, itself not verifiable at P3

claim: The daily load is 16 Wh against the 29.8 Wh/day of the TRL 2 estimate
law: Cross-check of the bottom-up build-up against the earlier lumped estimate (PIR gating and IA-21 duty explain the drop)

claim: A two-person crew installs one assembly on an existing pole in 2 hours or less
law: Sum of task times for clamps, bar and sign, enclosure, battery and wiring, panel, button, radar (estimate)

claim: A 70 x 40 mm solar tile keeps a road stud flashing 20 s per crossing, 300 times a day
law: Tile at 15 % and 2.5 peak sun hours stores 0.80 Wh/day; LEDs 0.35 plus a radio listening all day 0.44 Wh/day

claim: A stud's raised lens ring carries a wheel of a heavy axle
law: Wheel load over the 2,800 mm2 lens ring; polycarbonate compressive yield about 60 MPa (assumed), safety factor 1.5

claim: Studs at road level (antenna gain -3 dBi, 10 dB ground loss) hear the bollard across 15 m
law: Free-space path loss with extra ground-reflection and blockage allowances (estimate)

claim: The released panel stops from a 250 mm fall below 20 g, with the peak taken as twice the mean (end-of-travel damper, 25 mm stroke, CRS-DDR-005)
law: a = v^2 / (2 s) for v = sqrt(2 g h), times 2 for a real damper curve; the 20 g limit protects sheeting and fixings (assumed)

claim: A person lifts the panel with a pull of 22 N or less
law: Weight over pulley efficiency plus 10 % guide friction; 22.2 N is 5 lbf, the ADA operable-part force

claim: A retroreflective panel is seen by a driver at night without electricity
law: Retroreflective sheeting returns headlight beams to the driver; it needs no power, but the return depends on the sheeting class, the dirt and the panel angle
check: No calculation at P3; sheeting datasheet to assess
